page: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processors operating at 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 208 vCPUs across 104 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with an extensive 5700.0 GB of system memory, translating to 27.4 GB of RAM per core, and includes 8389 GB of local storage. No GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The server achieves top-tier status in multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU metrics, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, scoring in the top 10% for both cached small-block reads and large-block uncached read and write operations. Redis SET operations also reach top-tier throughput. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%.

Given the massive memory footprint and high multi-core throughput, this server is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It is highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, massive data warehousing, and complex enterprise resource planning systems. While the hardware class represents a significant resource density, the qualitative cost efficiency is optimized for workloads that can fully leverage the 5.7 TB of RAM and high-throughput multi-threaded processing, whereas single-threaded applications will underutilize the hardware.
